task-intent.statement: Add a concurrency test (TF9) driving real concurrent file I/O -- threads doing actual reads and writes, not mocks -- against the runner-durability work in epic-178.

expected-behavior.statement: The concurrency test would run to completion and report pass or fail like any other test in the suite.

observed-behavior.statement: TF9 hung the entire pytest process indefinitely. A writer thread died on a transient Windows os.replace sharing violation without signalling stop, leaving a non-daemon reader thread spinning forever.

impact-cost.statement: The whole pytest process hung rather than failing, so the failure did not surface as a test result. Wall-clock cost not recorded. 7 green re-runs followed the fix. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 2, confirmed 1, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-07-19 (epic-198-burndown), 9 runs since.

workaround.statement: Give the harness the same fail-safe discipline as the production code under test: wrap per-iteration work in try/except with a guaranteed stop-signal in `finally`, and mark helper threads daemon=True as a backstop.

task-intent.statement: Plan a bounded issue as a delegated commander working from a frozen Admiral launch order. Recurred across epics 152/154, epic-226 (wt-227, wt-230), 301, 300, 299 and issue-309.

expected-behavior.statement: The launch order's named defect, sub-fix or edit target would exist at the named address in current code, so planning could proceed from the order as given.

observed-behavior.statement: Six confirmations across three epics, in four distinct failure modes. (1) The named mechanism was ALREADY SHIPPED -- 152, 154, and epic-226 wt-227 twice. (2) A named EDIT TARGET did not exist under that name -- 'the Decision Anchors section of commander-core.md' (epic-226 wt-230). (3) The named baseline existed but was materially WEAKER than the order's framing implied: in 300, grepping showed the grounding covered deterministic SELECTION only and that ASSEMBLY did not exist at all. (4) A settled pre-ruling's LABEL was contradicted by the corpus itself: in 299, f1Brainz CLAUDE.md:7 already named docs/architecture/index.md as the canonical entrypoint, so the order's 'no canonical entrypoint' arm label was false. A fifth shape appeared in issue-309: the stale premise came not from the order's own text but from a DIFFERENT frozen project doc the order pointed at as a map substitute.

impact-cost.statement: Every instance was caught BEFORE planning by grepping the named symbol or token, so no rework is attributable to any of them. In 300 the check converted an extension gate aimed at a mechanism that was never there into a correctly-scoped build; in 299 it also corrected a stated corpus size from 5928 to 6435. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 9, confirmed 6, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-08-01 (issue-309), 1 run since -- the most-confirmed entry in the bank and never disconfirmed.

workaround.statement: Before planning, grep the launch order's NAMED defect or sub-fix against current code, AND verify that any named EDIT TARGET (section heading, file path, anchor) actually exists at the named address.

task-intent.statement: A crew was handed a task to observe a MID-process state -- a run stuck in 'launched' -- during the runner-durability work (#130).

expected-behavior.statement: The handoff's instructed discovery channel, a stderr line printed in a `finally` block, would reveal the kept temp dir.

observed-behavior.statement: The channel never fired. A hard Windows tree-kill skips `finally`, and a hanging subject never returns, so an END-of-process output channel cannot survive the very kill-or-hang being tested.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- the source lesson records no cost, no rework count and no wall-clock. The crew pivoted within the same dispatch. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 2, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 9 runs since banking -- an unknown recurrence count, not an absent one.

workaround.statement: The crew pivoted to a child-scoped TMP/TEMP environment variable -- a channel written before, and independently of, the death.

task-intent.statement: Fix a Stop-hook decision that depended on a harness-supplied `cwd` field, and write the regression test for it (stop-rail-151).

expected-behavior.statement: Unit tests using a hand-injected `cwd` fixture would demonstrate the fix works.

observed-behavior.statement: A cold critic found the fix rode an unverified assumption that Stop carries `cwd` at all; injected-cwd tests pass green even if production never delivers the field, hiding a silent no-op fix. Confirmed five times. A later confirm (governor-261) found that presence and LIVENESS are different questions: the docs confirmed `cwd` is present on every hook event, but a real non-fixture reproduction showed its SCOPE was wrong -- session-lifetime-fixed, not per-call-live -- for a Commander-in-worktree dispatch.

impact-cost.statement: In governor-261, verifying presence alone would have shipped a cwd-routing design that was a provable no-op; it was considered and rejected mid-run on that evidence. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 6, confirmed 5, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-07-27 (governor-268), 5 runs since.

workaround.statement: Verify the field's presence against the harness contract (docs) AND make the regression test drive the REAL writer path that populates it -- run handle_post_tool_use to write the binding, then decide_stop -- rather than a hand-injected fixture.

task-intent.statement: Ship `grade_lint.py` with 18 tests, including a four-template round-trip over the real shipped artifacts (epic-226 wt-230).

expected-behavior.statement: A round-trip test that lints and parses the REAL shipped artifacts would establish that the linter itself is correct.

observed-behavior.statement: All 18 passed while a greedy-placeholder regex silently PASSED an ungraded decision and a nested sub-bullet false-FAILed a valid plan -- both unreachable from the shipped templates. Confirmed three times over three different tools: checklist_engine's Inv3ExclusionCheck claimed totality over an excluded-verb set while exercising 4 of 10, surviving two rounds of a rework loop hunting exactly this class; #301's line-boundary guard rejected only backslash-n and backslash-r while the parser sectioned with str.splitlines(), so a U+2028 value passed validation, forged the exact status line the guard existed to prevent, and silently truncated the record; and #300 promoted a same-tree regenerate-and-compare round trip ABOVE the discriminating cross-environment check, in a plan whose own constraints array already quoted this lesson.

impact-cost.statement: In #301 the defect was found only because the reviewer was told to AUTHOR adversarial inputs rather than re-run the suite; a second #301 instance made the most natural caller idiom return the wrong episode. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 4, confirmed 3, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-08-01 (300), 2 runs since.

workaround.statement: Pair every round-trip or enumeration test over real artifacts with adversarial fixtures authored to make the tool return a WRONG answer -- false FAIL on a valid input, silent PASS on an invalid one -- and instruct reviewers to hunt that specific class rather than only re-running the suite.

task-intent.statement: Advance a Commander gate from a dispatched child checklist using `checklist_engine.py advance <gate> --from-child <path>` (epic-226 wt-228, and independently wt-231 in the same wave).

expected-behavior.statement: `--from-child` would accept the child checklist path the way every other engine verb used in these runs does, and would work against the child whatever its type.

observed-behavior.statement: Two undocumented behaviours. (1) It refuses a path to the child given relative to cwd, accepting only an absolute path -- unlike every other engine verb used in these runs. (2) It only works when the child checklist is a SURVEY type, because it needs a `consolidation` object to attach as review-result; against a GATED-type child such as execute.json it refuses with 'has no consolidation yet'. Neither behaviour is documented in --help or in the gate-execution doctrine, and the REFUSED message itself names neither rule.

impact-cost.statement: Forced a manual attest-plus-advance instead. Two independent worktrees hit the identical defect in one wave, resolved as one recurrence on a single stable identity rather than two adds. Constellation-scoped, so a confirm is DEBT rather than trust: recurrences 1, status `exported` (2026-07-24), upstream fix -- a REFUSED message naming the rule inline -- still unpaid at migration. mentions 2, confirmed 0, 8 runs since last confirm.

workaround.statement: Pass an absolute path, and fall back to a manual attest-plus-advance when the child checklist is GATED rather than SURVEY.

task-intent.statement: Close out an epic by sweeping Commander worktrees after harvesting their staged feedback (epic-226 closeout).

expected-behavior.statement: Doctrine already states 'harvest first, then remove' (constellation-admiral/SKILL.md, Closeout step 4), so the sweep would not run ahead of the harvest.

observed-behavior.statement: Nothing mechanically checks the harvest before a worktree sweep. A staged-feedback/<work-id>/ trio that passes its own Commander's feedback/archive gate -- which verifies only the STAGING copy -- looks identical from the outside to 'harvested and merged into the durable log', and is not the same thing. A second independent occurrence landed in the same evidence window: f1Brainz epic-601, where 6 of 6 staged trios were the sole surviving copy of their worktrees' learning before a human caught it and hand-merged.

impact-cost.statement: f1Brainz epic-601 was a real data-loss-narrowly-averted event, caught by a human rather than by any check. Constellation-scoped debt: recurrences 1, status `exported` (2026-07-24), the named upstream fix (a harvest-completeness mode in verify_agent_feedback.py) still unpaid at migration. mentions 2, confirmed 0, 8 runs since.

workaround.statement: epic-226's own preventive extra-diligence workaround: write explicit HARVEST EXECUTED and HARVEST MANIFEST entries into the Admiral log before any sweep runs.

task-intent.statement: Plan gates for bounded issues whose acceptance depends on a before/after measurement or a required round-trip or parser test -- epic-226 wt-227 and wt-230, then 300, 299 and issue-309.

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- the source lesson records no prior expectation. The cold plan critic was optional (bias-to-yes) at the time, so nothing was predicted about what it would find.

observed-behavior.statement: Every run that ran it found a plan-invalidating defect before any crew was dispatched. wt-227: an over-read baseline that would have been unproducible after g1/g2 overwrote the engine. wt-230: an undefined Markdown decision-line grammar that would have broken the issue's own required round-trip test. 300: two postconditions returning exit 0 with nothing built -- a bash negation bound to the collection probe rather than the lint, and a grep already matching 10 lines. 299: 8 blocking and 9 serious findings on a frozen measurement rubric, including two defects in the MEASURING INSTRUMENT itself. issue-309: 2 blocking and 3 serious, on a recall/noise measurement.

impact-cost.statement: Directly attributable counterfactuals in 300, 299 and issue-309: without the critic, vacuous acceptance checks would have shipped as evidence behind headline numbers, and 299's arm would have been captured, been unrecoverable, and read as a strong result. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 4, confirmed 3, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-08-01 (issue-309), 1 run since. This run, #308, is a further instance: the mandatory cold critic returned 2 BLOCKING findings on this issue's own gate plan.

workaround.statement: Run the cold plan critic as MANDATORY rather than bias-to-yes for any gate plan whose acceptance depends on a before/after measurement or a required round-trip or parser test.

task-intent.statement: Write a test that makes a candidate executable genuinely unresolvable, by passing a restricted env={'PATH': ...} into subprocess.run() (epic-226 wt-228).

expected-behavior.statement: Passing a restricted PATH through the child `env=` dict would control which executable an unqualified command name resolves to.

observed-behavior.statement: On Windows it does not. CreateProcess resolves the executable name against the CALLING process's real environment, not the child `env=` dict. The test looks correct and passes silently even when the probe logic is completely broken. Established empirically by two pasted `py -c` transcripts comparing env={'PATH': d} against mutating os.environ['PATH'] directly.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- no cost, rework count or wall-clock is recorded. Discovered empirically on one host and one Windows build; a single occurrence. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 8 runs since -- an unknown recurrence count.

workaround.statement: Mutate the ambient os.environ['PATH'] directly rather than passing a restricted `env=` override.

task-intent.statement: Author a gate postcondition that must prove a command CORRECTLY FAILS -- 'the guard refuses this input' (epic-226 wt-229).

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- no prior expectation is recorded. The lesson records the mismatch itself: the engine's command-postcondition semantics treat exit 0 as pass, which has no direct expression for a required refusal.

observed-behavior.statement: A gate that must prove a refusal has no direct expression in the engine's postcondition semantics, so it falls back to a self-reported attest. Confirmed once in 303: three command postconditions using the negation wrapper, all satisfied on first advance with no rework, with the verbatim commands, exit codes and stderr recorded in notes-303.md.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- no rework is attributable and no cost is recorded. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 2, confirmed 1, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-08-01 (303), 3 runs since.

workaround.statement: Use a `! <command>` bash-negation wrapper as the postcondition's `command` field, which turns 'the guard fired' into a mechanically re-verified engine check instead of a self-reported attest.

task-intent.statement: Plan a gate under a launch order that fenced a contended file during a concurrent wave (epic-226 wt-230).

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- none recorded. The order carried a stop-and-float instruction firing on 'another PR touches this file', with no stated expectation about the outcome.

observed-behavior.statement: Resolving the canonical target first made the contended edit unnecessary: under a PR-6-style canonical-source rule the content belonged in a different home, so the collision dissolved rather than needing resolution.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- nothing beyond the floated decision is recorded. A single occurrence. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 8 runs since -- an unknown recurrence count.

workaround.statement: Resolve the canonical target FIRST when a launch order fences a contended file, and qualify the stop-condition wording with 'if the edit is still required after canonical routing'.

task-intent.statement: Dispatch an implementer crew whose own driven plan file (<gate>-plan.json) was created directly in the work-id root .agent-work/<work-id>/ (governor-261, g1-implement-rework2).

expected-behavior.statement: The dispatched crew's plan file would resolve to its own Context Governor gauge, reflecting the crew's own context use.

observed-behavior.statement: checklist_engine.py's _gauge_path keys purely off the checklist file's own containing directory, so the crew's plan file resolved to the SAME gauge.json as the Commander's spine.json. Two consecutive attempts tripped the Governor's HARD band at m0-context before any code change, both traced to a shared gauge holding claude-opus-5 readings while both the Commander and its implementer ran Sonnet -- the reading belonged to the epic's own Admiral, which shared this Commander's session_id and physical transcript.

impact-cost.statement: Two consecutive dispatch attempts lost to a HARD trip before any real work was done. Independently confirmed and posted to issue #266. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 7 runs since.

workaround.statement: Place crew plan files in their own subdirectory, mirroring the reviewer role's <gate>-review/ convention, so they get their own gauge.json. A third attempt using .agent-work/governor-261/g1-implement-rework2-attempt3/ completed cleanly on the same task.

task-intent.statement: A reviewer needed to independently reproduce an OLD-versus-NEW behaviour contrast -- proving a bug is fixed by showing the old code reproduces it and the new code does not (governor-261, g1-review-rework2).

expected-behavior.statement: The standard technique -- temporarily edit the real file under review, run, then revert -- would work.

observed-behavior.statement: The permission classifier blocked it: a reviewer editing the artifact it is reviewing, reasonably flagged. The reviewer then improvised a working alternative within the same dispatch.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- no cost or rework is recorded; the reviewer solved it in-dispatch. A single occurrence. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 7 runs since.

workaround.statement: Write a reviewer-side standalone script that loads the real module by file path (importlib) and defines the OLD handler inline as a local function, reusing the SAME real helpers the new code uses -- reproducing the contrast without ever mutating the file under review. The reviewer explicitly recommended promoting it as the documented default.

task-intent.statement: Run a launch-order-mandated class sweep for the STATE_NOTE-fallback doctrine pattern (governor-268, LAUNCH_ORDER-268 part 2).

expected-behavior.statement: The existing regression drill (docs/superpowers/drills/dogfood-context-paths-absent.md) reporting PASS would mean the doctrine pattern was fixed across the whole class of sibling templates.

observed-behavior.statement: The drill names only ONE of several sibling role-templates carrying the pattern (the Commander spine, PR #75/#86). The sweep found skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md:57 carrying the identical missing-fallback defect, undetected, while the drill kept reporting PASS.

impact-cost.statement: The Admiral spine carried the same unfixed defect indefinitely until this sweep found it -- the drill could not have surfaced it by re-running. A single instance, one doctrine pattern, one drill. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 5 runs since.

workaround.statement: When authoring or updating a drill for a doctrine pattern that recurs across sibling templates, enumerate every sibling template carrying the pattern in the drill's 'doctrine under test' line, or explicitly note which ones it does NOT cover.

task-intent.statement: Run a lightweight design-it-twice pass (2 candidates, single-context, not a full panel) plus one solo cold-critic subagent on a bounded single-issue plan whose design space the pre-rulings had already narrowed (governor-265).

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- none recorded. The run had judged a full panel unnecessary; no prediction about what the lightweight pass would find is written down.

observed-behavior.statement: It caught a genuine blocking design gap -- an undesigned fan-out and clearing scope for a new multi-path sidecar -- before the implement gate started.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- no cost is recorded; the gap was caught pre-implement so no rework is attributable. A single data point from one run. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 4 runs since.

workaround.statement: Keep the lightweight design-it-twice pass plus one solo cold critic as a default floor even when a run judges a full panel unnecessary.

task-intent.statement: A reviewer crew executed the installed constellation-reviewer skill's r6-fowler step (governor-265).

expected-behavior.statement: The imperative's instruction -- record the Fowler pass 'to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json' -- would name an unambiguous destination.

observed-behavior.statement: Read literally, the instruction means overwriting the shared skill template rather than filling a per-run working copy. The reviewer inferred a working-copy fill, mirroring how review.json itself works, but had to reason past the ambiguous wording to get there.

impact-cost.statement: UNKNOWN -- no rework or cost is recorded; the reviewer reasoned past it. The named target is upstream of this repo -- the installed constellation-reviewer skill's r6-fowler wording, not a file this repo owns -- and delegated mode could not self-apply a doctrine fix that run. Constellation-scoped. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 4 runs since.

workaround.statement: The reviewer inferred a per-run working-copy fill from how review.json behaves and proceeded on that reading.

task-intent.statement: Write a validator in the episode store's writer (#301) protecting a downstream parser from a free-text field forging a store status line.

expected-behavior.statement: Rejecting values containing backslash-n or backslash-r would block the injection the guard existed to prevent.

observed-behavior.statement: Two instances in the same run, in different costumes. At g2, the parser sectioned files with str.splitlines(), which also breaks on vertical tab, form feed, the file/group/record separators, NEL, U+2028 and U+2029 -- so a U+2028 value passed validation, forged the exact '- status: retired' line the guard existed to prevent, and silently dropped everything after the separator on the next touch; the reviewer demonstrated it end to end. At g4, binding the ratified file-move retirement layout moved membership from file CONTENT to file LOCATION, and the non-episode classifier was a hand-maintained filename allowlist consulted only at the flat root while both scanned directories were globbed unconditionally -- so the store as shipped could not be read by its own tooling, and its own README placeholders became a phantom episode id in both directories at once. Also observed, as a record that someone wrote it and deciding nothing, the lesson's author at banking time: 'The tell is identical both times: a list a human maintains standing in for a predicate the code can decide.'

impact-cost.statement: The g4 instance was a cold-panel BLOCK, reproduced by the commander in one command (`python scripts/query_episodes.py enumerate` erroring against the store the gate ships). The g2 instance silently truncated records. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 2 runs since.

workaround.statement: Replace the hand-maintained list with the computable property the code already owns. For the parser guard, the predicate 'value is non-empty and value.splitlines() != [value]', which cannot drift because it IS the parser's behaviour -- noting the trailing-separator case, where a length check alone is insufficient because a value ending in a separator splits to one element. For the classifier, the store's own id grammar (episode_id_for()), applied uniformly to both directories.

task-intent.statement: Run a design-it-twice panel -- #301 with four candidates, #300 with three authors -- and read its convergences as evidence.

expected-behavior.statement: Convergence across deliberately-differing candidates would be evidence that the converged claim is sound.

observed-behavior.statement: A panel varies what it is told to vary and inherits everything it is not, from TWO different sources. In #301 all four candidates inherited from PRIOR ART the claim that .agent-work/ is gitignored; `git check-ignore .agent-work/episodes/` exiting 0 and `git ls-files .agent-work/` returning zero were false at the time of use. In #300 the panel's own shared-assumption audit retracted a 'metadata only, never file content' convergence after finding it was the BRIEF handed back rather than independent agreement, and separately found that all three authors had verified the blob-OID identity only under the current '* text=auto' .gitattributes with no -text or binary exemption -- a silent-divergence hazard in the one primitive the whole manifest rests on. Neither inheritance is visible in how the candidates differ, so convergence cannot surface either. Also observed, as a record that someone wrote it and deciding nothing, the lesson's author at banking time: 'all three are failures about what candidates SHARE rather than how they differ, and in each case agreement read as evidence when it was only inheritance.'

impact-cost.statement: #301's inheritance was corrected in the amend authority on execute.json and in docs/EPISODE_STORE.md section 1. #300's audit retracted one of five reported convergences, found an unquestioned inherited declaration location (filed as an obligation onto #306), and closed the .gitattributes hazard as postcondition g1-implement.c7, verified in both directions -- exit 0 today, exit 1 after appending '*.md -text', tree restored. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 2, confirmed 1, disconfirmed 0, last confirmed 2026-08-01 (300), 2 runs since.

workaround.statement: Run a shared-assumption audit over the panel's convergences, by an auditor who did NOT author the brief, and treat unanimity across deliberately-differing constraints as evidence about the varied axis only.

task-intent.statement: Verify work across epic-298 using guards, gate postconditions and tests.

expected-behavior.statement: A green check would mean the thing it checks was actually verified.

observed-behavior.statement: Five or more instances in one epic by different mechanisms. (1) #301's floor-interpreter guard discovered an interpreter BY NAME, found none, and SKIPPED -- green, zero coverage. (2) #300 found two postconditions that passed vacuously. (3) round-trip tests that only ever see clean shipped artifacts cannot catch a parser bug. (4) In 299 the MUTATION TEST itself was the check that could not fail: a sed-applied mutant silently did not match, the file was unchanged, the suite stayed green, and 'mutant killed' was the natural misreading -- exposed only by separately asserting the mutation had applied; in the same run the self-test's fixtures used only input.command, so the extractor's real field-extraction path was never exercised until a real stream-json excerpt was checked in. (5) In issue-309 a `git status --porcelain` check over a gitignored directory passed unconditionally whether or not the slice was seeded, and a not-found-id test stood in for a guard-fired test.

impact-cost.statement: In 299 the vacuous mutation test would have let a broken measuring instrument read as a strong result across all five runs. Constellation-scoped debt: recurrences 2, status `exported`, exported twice on 2026-08-01 (for 299 and for issue-309) each carrying the originating lesson id so the upstream sweep groups on stable identity. The suggested upstream edit recorded at export: extend the repair clause to 'mutate, ASSERT THE MUTATION APPLIED, then watch it go red', and require a fixture captured from the real format for any guard over an external format. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 3, confirmed 0, recurrences 2, last confirmed 2026-08-01 (issue-309), 1 run since.

workaround.statement: Require the check to demonstrate it actually ran against something that could have failed it: accept an interpreter only if it REPORTS the floor version when asked; author an adversarial fixture for a test; use a bash-negation proving the guard fires for a postcondition. Mutation-testing a guard -- break the thing, watch it go red, restore -- is the cheap general form, and the mutation must itself be asserted to have applied.

task-intent.statement: Coordinate multi-agent work in which one agent uses a description another agent took earlier -- #301's design panel, and the epic-298 Admiral's sibling-fork resolution at harvest.

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- the source lesson records no prior expectation; it is written as a distinction between two shapes rather than as a single incident with an expectation.

observed-behavior.statement: A description accurate when taken and wrong when used comes in TWO shapes with DIFFERENT fixes. Shape 1 yields to verification: agent_work_root.py:136-141 versus its own docstring; `git ls-files .agent-work/` returning zero against all four #301 candidates; .gitattributes containing '* text=auto', corrected on issue #319. Shape 2 does not: the epic-298 Admiral's fork resolution named design-candidates-inherit-the-neighbours-assumptions-without-checking-them AFTER it had been renamed to a-panel-inherits-what-it-was-not-told-to-vary -- a fact shared between two agents that neither could see the other write -- caught before harvest only by comparing the live staged file. Also observed, as a record that someone wrote it and deciding nothing, the lesson's author at banking time: 'this op and [a-panel-inherits-what-it-was-not-told-to-vary] were BOTH deliberately kept whole rather than split, for the same reason -- their halves have UNEQUAL FIX COSTS, so the cheap half (the one with an obvious mechanical mitigation) is the half that gets fixed alone and the class declared closed. Twice in one wave the right call was refuse to split a lesson whose halves have unequal fix costs. That generalization may outlive both lessons.'

impact-cost.statement: Shape 2 cost a near-miss on its first occurrence; the same Admiral's protective snapshot captured the superseded delta. Constellation-scoped, because shape 2 is a property of the multi-agent machinery itself -- it appears only where two agents share a fact neither can see the other write, which is the worktree-and-harvest topology this corpus runs on. Playbook counters at migration: mentions 1, confirmed 0, disconfirmed 0, last-confirmed none, 2 runs since.

workaround.statement: For shape 2, a quote-id-and-count protocol: compare the live staged file before harvest rather than trusting a name taken earlier. Shape 1 is covered by ordinary verification. The lesson's author explicitly warns against graduating shape 1 alone and considering the class closed.

task-intent.statement: Plan #308's g5 gate: cut live agents off from the lessons bank, by enumerating every artifact under skills/ that instructs an agent to read LESSONS.md, and write a guard asserting the cut. Corpus at 4cec87a, role commander, spine step plan.

expected-behavior.statement: The hand-written enumeration of lesson-intake sites in the gate imperative would be complete, and the guard written against it would fail if any live intake site survived.

observed-behavior.statement: While planning the consolidation of a cluster whose shared failure mode is an under-inclusive or stale secondhand claim taken as premise, the commander committed that exact failure mode twice within roughly one hour. First, the g5 imperative enumerated 5 live-agent lesson-intake sites as though complete; a command over the corpus finds 6 across 5 files -- the missed one is in ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json, in the `latitude` task rather than `context`, so a reader checking `context` would also have missed it. Second, one revision later and inside the guard written to fix that, the character class [^.backslash-n]{0,40} excludes the dot and so could never match any phrase containing '.agent-work/'; it went green against three live intake sites. Also observed, as a record that someone wrote it and deciding nothing, the commander's own conclusion at the time: 'prose did not stop an agent that had just read the cluster, was actively consolidating it, and had the remedy in front of it -- that is a real argument for bin 1 and against my own stated lean.' That conclusion is the kind of importance call Tommy has since ruled a local agent must not make; it is recorded here as something the author wrote, not as a finding.

impact-cost.statement: Recurrence count 2, same agent, within roughly one hour, under maximal awareness -- the agent had just finished writing down that this is a recurring failure mode. Both were caught: the first by a cold plan critic, the second by running the guard and reading which sites it named. No defective artifact reached a crew or a merge.

workaround.statement: Replace the hand-written enumeration with a script that enumerates the corpus itself and asserts the enumeration is non-empty -- .agent-work/issue-308/checks/lesson_intake_is_cut.py -- and verify a new guard by reading which sites it actually names, not by its exit code.

task-intent.statement: Run the first live rhyme-search over the episode store (7 active episodes, 0 retired, across 2 runs, at 4cec87a) to see whether it surfaces a cluster at all. An independent cold sensor was dispatched with fresh context, no hypothesis, and explicit authorisation to return 'no cluster'.

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- the run was set up to accept an honest null; no positive expectation was registered before the sensor ran.

observed-behavior.statement: The sensor found a cluster of three episodes across two runs and two roles, sharing the pattern: a written secondhand claim about current repo state was taken as a premise, was wrong, and only re-deriving it by command caught it. issue-304-g3-001 (implementer): a handoff enumerated the suites pinning a file; the enumeration was under-inclusive and two out-of-scope test files broke. issue-304-g3-003 (implementer): a handoff asserted a prior gate had already made a textual change; it had not, and reading the current file would have CONFIRMED the false claim -- only git log plus git show over the 8 commits touching the file disproved it. issue-309-002 (commander): docs/EPISODE_STORE.md section 1's worked git check-ignore transcript claimed .agent-work/ was ignored -- true when written at #301, invalidated by #326 -- and the plan's first draft inherited the false premise. The cluster independently rediscovered a pattern LESSONS.md already held (lesson:verify-launch-order-claims-against-code, mentions 9 / confirmed 6), by a different route with no access to that file.

impact-cost.statement: Observed facts about the two candidate remedies, used to decide nothing: a mechanical doc-transcript checker would have caught 1 of the 3 members (only issue-309-002 is a machine-checkable transcript); a prose instruction addresses 3 of 3, and each episode's own proposed-remedy independently converged on a variant of that sentence. The sensor ran BEFORE the commander recorded its own read, so agreement between them is convergence rather than inheritance. No consolidation was landed: Tommy withdrew the bin ruling, and deciding which observation deserves a doctrine line is the importance judgement he ruled requires a global view.

workaround.statement: UNKNOWN -- no workaround was applied. The consolidation this cluster was found for was withdrawn mid-run, so the cluster is recorded as an observation only.

task-intent.statement: Same rhyme-search pass as the cluster-A observation: one solo read by the commander, plus an independent cold sensor over the same 7 episodes.

expected-behavior.statement: UNKNOWN -- no positive expectation was registered; the sensor was authorised to return no cluster.

observed-behavior.statement: The sensor found a second strong cluster the commander's solo read had MISSED -- the solo read had grouped issue-304-g3-005 as a singleton. Shared pattern: a check reports without being able to register the outcome it is credited with detecting, and in both instances the instrument was operated by the party whose work it measured. issue-304-g3-005: 'the measured defect -- lateness -- remains unenforced'; the check 'ran BY THE AGENT WHO AUTHORED THE ANCHOR'; it 'can verify that orientation HAPPENED but can never verify that it happened FIRST'. issue-309-001: 'a null is not a demonstration'; 'the 0% noise result measures lens discipline, not an absence of noise risk in the underlying pathway'. This cluster is the episode-store rediscovery of lesson:a-check-that-cannot-fail-is-indistinguishable-from-one-that-passed, reached independently with no access to LESSONS.md, and it adds a shape that lesson does not carry: SELF-MEASUREMENT.

impact-cost.statement: A data point about the rhyme-search pathway itself: one read is not enough to trust a null on any individual cluster. #308's honest-null clause covers the store-wide result; a per-cluster miss is a different and quieter failure, and it happened here. Filed as issue #392 rather than consolidated, so it was not silently dropped when decision:one-consolidation-not-many bound the run to one.

workaround.statement: Dispatch an independent cold sensor in addition to the solo read, and treat the solo read's singletons as unconfirmed rather than as negatives. The candidate instruction as the sensor phrased it, recorded as the sensor's words and deciding nothing: 'before a check counts as evidence, state the condition under which it would FAIL and show it can reach that condition; if that condition is unobservable to the instrument, report a measurement gap, not a pass.'
